newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Senate begins debate on broadcasting bill.
newsitem.headline: French Senate begins debate on broadcasting bill.

text.p: The French Senate, the upper house of Parliament, is scheduled to debate on Wednesday and Thursday a bill to reform public broadcasting, to give a legal framework to satellite television and provide a new framework for radio.
The bill also contains provisions to adapt the remit of the French state broadcasting regulator, the Conseil Superieur de l'Audiovisuel (CSA), to include satellite television programme offerings.
The CSA on Monday complied with a government request to re-examine completely the use of the FM band and set up a commission to look into the matter.
The authority last week advised against overhauling the radio sector, but said it wanted to have additional means to correct certain imbalances. It gave no further details.

Satellite TV would have a sufficiently flexible framework to allow operators to develop, but there would be rules to avoid a concentration of television groups, Culture Minister Philippe Douste-Blazy, who is sponsoring the bill, said earlier this year.
Public television is likely to be the focus of the parliamentary debate, industry experts say.

The government plans to organise state-owned television in two groupings. The first would be centred on France Television, which would include the general channels, and specialist channels La Cinquieme, La Sept and Arte would form the second grouping.
La Cinquieme is an educational channel while La Sept and Arte give priority to cultural programmes. The government has said it plans to propose the merger of these channels in the Spring.

Once the senators have formulated their ammendments, the bill will return to the National Assembly (lower house of Parliament), then be vetted by the Conseil Constitutional, probably in the Summer, before becoming law.
